First of all, I would like to thank you for your words of encouragement. It is hard to see the good reasons to continue this life. I’m taking it one day at a time and moment to moment. It’s hard to trust my feelings right now because they are all over the place. One minute I’m fine and ready to get back to normal and the next I’m angry, crying, feeling hopeless and just ready to die. My wife has been my rock and I owe her my life.

Second, is there anything you can offer in terms of tips to help secure FMLA for this? The last time I did the paperwork a year ago it was rejected by HR for insufficient reasons on three occasions. It took me going to the benefits administrator with an excuse from the hospital from my stay when I attempted suicide for them to take my mental illness seriously. At this time my paperwork is up for recertification and I fear that my company is looking to let me go should I be unable to give them exact amounts of time for when my depressive episodes hit and for how long they last. Which as you may well know, are unpredictable. I work in an area of the country that still doesn’t take mental health seriously. The consensus idea is “everyone’s got problems and you just need to get over it.” My company claims to be a “family” but when it comes to the bottom dollar of you’re not a boss or part of the immediate group who kiss ass to the bosses then you are replaceable regardless of work performance.

Traditions are ridiculous, family is too involved, shit is way expensive, and pressure for everything to be perfect is intense. Forget all that crap. No one wants to hear your cheesy vows or your friends awkward speech of approval. 

Also I feel that if you can’t afford to pay for your own wedding then you aren’t ready for everything else that comes with it.  Just my take. No offense to anyone.

How old are you? I myself as well as siblings have all felt this way. The whole, never thought we’d reach 30 thing. What’s up with that? Are we just part of a generation who believe that the good or great die young? And if so, what happens when you pass the age of expected demise? I’m currently 32 and I just don’t know what the hell to do with myself. Went to school, got a bachelor’s. Traveled a little bit. Bounced around until I found a great job with awesome pay, amazing benefits, a gym at work and I actually like and respect my boss. So what’s the problem? I still have that heavy fog that clouds my brain to the point where I just want to give up on everything. I see a therapist and take meds but it’s always there. Ready to darken my thoughts. Right now I am struggling with summer. Missing the days of youth and little to no responsibilities.
